forces.title: AI reshaping GCCs to Global Intelligence Centers, reducing headcount
forces.description: AI is fundamentally transforming GCCs, potentially reducing headcount by 25-35% in three years and 55-65% in ten years while increasing value per person significantly (3-5x). This shifts GCCs from execution-focused centers to 'Global Intelligence Centers' focused on judgment, regulatory interpretation, and novel problem formulation. It demands a deliberate, phased transformation and skill recomposition rather than simple cost-cutting.

forces.title: Rising enterprise demand for AI, ML, and cybersecurity services
forces.description: Enterprises are increasingly prioritizing AI/ML and cybersecurity, viewing them as essential for productivity, resilience, and growth rather than experimental. This drives significant investment in technology services, ensuring tech services are a core component of IT budgets. Tech services firms that effectively integrate these capabilities with appropriate talent and commercial models are best positioned to win new, outcome-oriented opportunities.

forces.title: Client demand shifting IT services to outcome-based pricing
forces.description: Client demand for double-digit productivity improvements from AI and technology investments is pressuring the traditional FTE-based model in tech services. Clients are pushing for lower delivery costs, faster timelines, and outcome-based pricing. This necessitates tech services firms to redesign their pricing structures, automate delivery, reuse assets, and shift to platform-based delivery to ensure margin expansion and growth.

forces.title: Critical talent shortage for AI/ML engineering and cybersecurity skills
forces.description: Executives across industries cite cybersecurity, AI/ML engineering, and data science as among the hardest skills to source talent for. This talent gap presents a significant risk to tech services firms' ability to meet rising client demand for AI and security-led initiatives. Managed services are viewed as an antidote, bringing specialized talent, but buyers often undervalue this aspect, highlighting a misunderstanding of the required expertise.

forces.title: Managed services leveraged as critical AI acceleration and digital transformation driver
forces.description: Senior leaders are increasingly turning to managed services to accelerate AI adoption and drive strategic impact, moving beyond in-house development. AI capability is the most-cited consideration for managed services, followed by tech expertise. This model helps companies navigate AI complexity, bridge talent gaps, and achieve strategic outcomes like innovation, operational resilience, and agility, becoming a top investment priority.

forces.title: GCCs evolving into strategic innovation and value creation hubs
forces.description: Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are undergoing a significant transformation, evolving from cost-focused back-office units to strategic powerhouses and innovation hubs. They are increasingly taking on end-to-end process ownership, driving digital transformation, and enabling core industry functions across sectors like Retail, CPG, and Healthcare & Life Sciences. This shift emphasizes value generation, speed, digital-first execution, and strategic partnerships, moving beyond traditional IT and operational roles.

forces.title: Pharma/Life Sciences GCCs shorten drug development with AI, automation
forces.description: India's pharma and life sciences GCCs are significantly reducing drug development timelines and costs by leveraging AI, automation, and advanced analytics across the value chain. From faster protein design to improved patient recruitment and streamlined regulatory approvals, these centers eliminate operational bottlenecks. This efficiency frees R&D teams for high-impact innovation, leading to therapies reaching clinics faster and more affordable medicines, transforming GCCs into global health accelerators.

forces.title: BFSI's AI-enabled cyber risk and low readiness creates service demand
forces.description: Indian BFSI faces rapidly increasing cyber risks from AI-enabled threats (deepfake social engineering, GenAI data leakage), with cyber incidents doubling in four years. BFSI leaders show limited confidence in their readiness to withstand such attacks, and existing cyber defenses are built for human-paced threats. This significant gap, coupled with a critical cybersecurity talent shortage, creates a strong and urgent demand for specialized IT services firms offering advanced AI-enabled cybersecurity solutions and managed security services.

forces.title: India maintains strong IT talent pool for global services
forces.description: India boasts the world's largest developer workforce (5.4 million software engineers) and produces over 500,000 new graduates annually, ensuring a consistent influx of talent. The country also leads globally in AI talent acquisition, with a 33% annual hiring rate. This vast and growing talent pool is a crucial competitive advantage for India's IT services and GCCs, underpinning their ability to deliver complex projects and scale operations for global clients.

forces.title: Government initiatives boosting AI ecosystem and digital infrastructure
forces.description: The Indian government is actively supporting the IT and AI ecosystem through significant investments and policies. Initiatives like the IndiaAI Mission (Rs 10,372 crore outlay) foster AI development and create common compute platforms. Budget allocations for AI, digital infrastructure investments (approx. US$ 70 billion in progress), and tax holidays for cloud services enhance the operating environment. This proactive support stimulates innovation, strengthens infrastructure, and creates opportunities for IT services and GCCs.

viewpoints.title: India GCCs becoming strategic innovation hubs for Retail and CPG
viewpoints.description: EY states that India's GCCs for Retail and CPG have evolved from back-office support into strategic powerhouses driving innovation across core processes like merchandising, sales, marketing, and customer services. By combining scale, speed, and digital-first execution, leveraging advanced analytics, AI, ML, and automation, these centers empower global brands. They are becoming critical hubs for global retail transformation, managing end-to-end processes and enabling leadership to focus on strategy and growth.

viewpoints.title: India's Healthcare & Life Sciences GCCs transform into innovation engines
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights that Healthcare and Life Sciences GCCs in India have matured into powerful engines for scientific innovation, digital transformation, and measurable patient impact. India's talent, innovation ecosystem, and global operating benchmarks position it as a strategic hub. These GCCs are moving beyond cost efficiency to spearhead global initiatives in R&D, regulatory operations, and product engineering, contributing significantly to faster treatments and resilient supply chains globally.

viewpoints.title: AI to redefine GCCs: fewer people, higher value, strategic role
viewpoints.description: KPMG asserts AI will fundamentally reshape Global Capability Centres, leading to significant headcount reduction (e.g., 20k to 7k over 10 years) but dramatically increasing value per person (3-5x). GCCs will shift from execution to 'Global Intelligence Centres,' focusing on judgment and strategic thinking. This transformation is already in motion and requires deliberate, phased adaptation, not merely cost-cutting, to maintain strategic relevance and build talent advantage.

viewpoints.title: Tech services spending to increase, driven by AI and cybersecurity demand
viewpoints.description: Bain's survey indicates that despite flat overall IT budgets, spending on technology services is set to increase due to rising client demand for AI/ML and cybersecurity support. Enterprises are moving beyond experimentation, viewing AI as core to transformation and seeking measurable productivity gains. This reinforces tech services as essential, not discretionary, favoring firms that integrate AI, data, cloud, and security with strong talent and outcome-based commercial models.

viewpoints.title: GCCs vital for strategic trade credit management and liquidity via tech
viewpoints.description: EY highlights GCCs as crucial strategic tools for effective trade credit risk management, moving beyond internal control. They centralize data, standardize processes, and deploy technology (AI, analytics, automation) for real-time insights and governance across global enterprises. This enables smarter, scalable credit decisions, safeguards liquidity, and enhances profitability, transforming credit management from reactive to strategic, aligning with business priorities.

viewpoints.title: Managed services crucial for accelerating AI adoption and strategic impact
viewpoints.description: KPMG's survey reveals that senior leaders increasingly leverage managed services as an AI accelerator and driver of strategic impact, rather than solely building in-house. AI capability is the top consideration, followed by tech expertise and transformation mindset. Managed services are seen as critical for navigating AI complexity, bridging talent gaps, and achieving outcomes beyond cost savings, making it a strategic priority for nearly all organizations.

viewpoints.title: India's IT industry poised for strong growth, driven by digital transformation
viewpoints.description: IBEF reports that India's IT industry is on track to double its revenue to US$ 500 billion by 2030, with significant contributions from digital transformation, AI adoption, and cloud modernization. The IT services market alone is projected to reach US$ 42.7 billion in 2025, growing at a 6.94% CAGR to US$ 78.1 billion by 2034. This growth is supported by a robust talent pool, increasing investments, and strategic government policies.

demand_drivers.description: Focus on high-value collaborations with global clients, moving beyond transactional engagements.
Availability of a large and continuously growing skilled workforce in India.
Integration of AI in service delivery and product development, enhancing efficiency and offerings.
Expansion and deepening of GCC mandates in India, contributing to overall service exports.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected software services exports from India. IT services are identified as the major contributor, accounting for more than 65% of total IT exports.

demand_drivers.description: Increasing adoption of IT services by enterprises for various digital initiatives.
Companies investing in digital initiatives across various sectors including cloud migration, system integration, and IT consulting.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected market size for India's IT services, led by IT outsourcing.

pnl_drivers.description: Managed services optimize processes, reduce technical debt, and offer efficient AI and cloud operations, leading to significant cost savings (15-45%) and improved financial performance.

market_sizing.methodology: Managed services can potentially reduce total operating costs by 15% to 45%.
